construct: RANKL expressed by osteoblast-lineage/stromal cells binds RANK on osteoclast precursors and promotes osteoclast differentiation and activation. Osteoprotegerin (OPG), produced by osteoblasts/stromal cells, binds RANKL as a soluble decoy receptor and prevents RANK activation, thereby suppressing osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A soluble osteoblast-lineage product that binds RANKL and prevents RANK engagement is osteoprotegerin, the physiologic decoy receptor that suppresses osteoclastogenesis.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: RANK is central to the same pathway, but it is the membrane receptor on osteoclast precursors rather than a soluble RANKL-binding decoy.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The biochemical behavior stated in the stem is the defining function of osteoprotegerin.
